Total work = Efficiency × Time

because B makes tank empty.

questions.question: Find the work done (in kJ) if a force of 750 N pushes a cart of mass 30 kg by 16 m.
questions.solution:
__CONCEPT:__

__
 
• Work is said to be done by a force when the body is displaced actually through some distance in the direction of the applied force.
 
• Since the body is being displaced in the direction of F, therefore work done by the force in displacing the body through a distance s is given by

W = vec F · vec s

Or, W = Fs cos θ

 
• Thus work done by a force is equal to the scalar or dot product of the force and the displacement of the body.

**CALCULATION**__:

Given that:

*⇒ *Force, F = 750 N

*⇒ *displacement, s = 16 m

*⇒ *Work done, w = Fs Cos θ 

Here θ is zero degree so Cos θ = 1

*⇒ W* = 750 × 16

*⇒ W* = 12000 J

To convert Joule into Kilo Joule divide by 1000

*⇒ *w = 12000 / 1000

*⇒ ***Work done, W = 12 KJ**

*⇒ ****__Note:__***** **1 Joule = 0.001 Kilo Joule

The astronaut weighs 90 kgf on Earth. This means that the astronaut weighs 90 x 10 = 900 N (since under Earth's gravity 1kgf = 1N 10 m/s²).

 

On the moon, the acceleration due to gravity is 1/6 of that on Earth, so the astronaut's weight will be 1/6 of his weight on Earth.

 

This gives us 1/6 × 900 N = 150 N

 

So, the correct answer is: 150 N.

 

**An astronaut who weighs 90 kg on Earth will weigh 150 N on the moon**

questions.question: Find the efficiency of a pulley system which has a mechanical advantage of 2.5 and where the load lifts by 2.5 meters on pulling the rope by 10 m.

__**Concept:**__

**Mechanical advantage:**

__
 
• It is a number that tells us how many times a simple machine multiplies the effort force. 
 
• is defined as the **ratio of output force to input force.**
 
• The mechanical advantage of a machine gives its efficiency. 
 
• Formula, MA=(F₀)/(F_i), where, F₀ = output force, Fᵢ = input force
 
• It is a unitless and dimensionless quantity.

**Efficiency:**

 
• The efficiency of a machine is the **ratio of the work done on the load by the machine to the work done on the machine by the effort.**
 
• Thus, it is the ratio of useful work done by the machine output to the work done by the machine input.
 
• It is represented by the Greek symbol η.
 
• Formula, efficiency, eta=(mechanical advantage)/(velocity ratio)

Velocity ratio:

 
• The ratio of the distance moved by the point at which the effort is applied in a simple machine to the distance moved by the point at which the load is applied at the same time.
 
• Formula, velocity ratio=(distance moved by effort)/(distance moved by load)
 
• In the case of an ideal (frictionless and weightless) machine, velocity ratio = mechanical advantage.

**Calculation:**__

Given: mechanical advantage, MA = 2.5, length of load lift, LR = 2.5 m, length of effort, LE = 10 m

Velocity ratio, v=(10)/(2.5)=4

Efficiency, eta=(mechanical advantage)/(velocity ratio)

eta=(2.5)/(4)=0.625

**In percentage, the efficiency is 62.50 %.**

• The act or science of measuring the changes in the state variables of a body in order to calculate the heat transfer associated with changes in its states, such as physical changes or phase transitions under specific conditions, is known as calorimetry.
 
• Calorimetry is performed with the help of a calorimeter.

**Calorimetry Principle:**

 
• When two bodies of different temperatures are placed in physical contact with each other, the heat is transferred from the body with a higher temperature to the body with a lower temperature until thermal equilibrium is attained between them.
 
• The body at a higher temperature releases heat while the body at a lower temperature absorbs heat.
 
• **The principle of calorimetry indicates the law of conservation energy,** i.e. the total heat lost by the hot body is equal to the total heat gained by the cold body.
 
• **Heat Lost = Heat Gained**
 
• 
 
**The heat transfer in a system is calculated using the formula, Q = mcΔT**, Where Q = the measure of heat transfer, m = the mass of the body, c = the specific heat of the body, Δt = the change in the temperature

 
 
• 
 
The final temperature of the mixture is given as, T=(m₁s₁T₁+m₂s₂T₂)/(m₁s₁+m₂s₂), where T represents temperature, m represents mass and the s represents the specific heat

T=(m₁s₁T₁+m₂s₂T₂)/(m₁s₁+m₂s₂)

Here, s₁ = s₂ = s (specific heat)

T=(m₁T₁+m₂T₂)/(m₁+m₂)

T=(0.5times 90+ 3.5times 10)/(0.5+3.5)

T = 20 ºC

**Hence, the final equilibrium temperature is 20 ºC.**

questions.question: In a multi split AC system ________

options.text: You can set different temperatures for different rooms
Temperature controls are installed in each room
You cannot set different temperatures for different rooms
You cannot control temperature by single temperature controller

questions.solution:
__**Explanation:**__

**Multi-split AC systems:**

 
• A multi-split type air conditioning system operates on the same principles as a split-type air-conditioning system.
 
• However in this case there are multiple evaporator units connected to one external condensing unit.
 
• These simple systems were designed mainly for small to medium commercial applications where the installation of ductwork was either too expensive or aesthetically unacceptable.
 
• The small-bore refrigerant piping, which connects the indoor and outdoor units require much lower space and are easier to install than the metal ducting.
 
• Each indoor unit has its own set of refrigerant pipework connecting it to the outdoor unit.
 
• The fact that one large condenser can be connected to multiple evaporators within the building reduces and/or eliminates the need for ductwork installation completely.
 
• Multi-splits are suitable for single thermal zone applications with very similar heat gains/losses.
 
• **In a multi-split AC system, you can set different temperatures for different rooms.**

**Multi-split unit Air conditioning working:**

 
• Like any form of air conditioning multi-split unit air conditioning works by extracting heat from the air of a room and discharging it outdoors.
 
• A multi-split unit air conditioning, however, is so called because it “splits” the cold unit- the “evaporator” coil which is located indoors from the hot unit- the condenser and compressor which are located outdoors, usually in a weather-proof metal cabinet, for greater efficiency and less noise.
 
• A chemical is known as a “refrigerant” which is easily transformed from liquid to gas, and back again, is pumped through the evaporator coil where it absorbs heat energy as well as moisture from the air in a room.
 
• The cool, dehumidified, air is circulated back into the room and the heat is carried away by the refrigerant to the outdoor unit where it is discharged.
 
• The refrigerant itself is compressed so that it once again becomes a low-pressure liquid and the cycle is repeated until optimum air temperature is attained.

**Retrofitting of CFC-filled refrigerator with the HFC 134a refrigerant:**

 
• Retrofit is a process where a defective CFC system refrigerator can be changed to HFC 134a charged system by converting mechanical fitting and taking precautionary steps.
 
• **When retrofitting a CFC-12 system to an HFC-134a system, fitting adaptors and a label must be installed or replaced.**

• First access the refrigerator to be retrofitted with HFCs.

• The hoses and tools used for charging and oil charging should be separate for the HFCs unit since these tools get cross contaminated if used with other units using CFCs or HCs.
 
• Also, the oil used in HFCs is hygroscopic (High moisture absorbent).
 
• Hence strict vigil and concentration are to be taken while using the tools and equipment.
 
• Now attach the pierce valve to the charge line and connect the recovery machine to the charge line and pump out the CFC 12 in the system.
 
• Remove the compressor (removing leg bolts, and motor leads) by cutting open copper tubes using a tubing cutter.
 
• Also strip out the condenser, capillary tube, and filter strainer.
 
• Immediately plug all the ends of the copper tubing of the components and the system to avoid moisture entering the system.
 
• And change with a new compressor that has polyester oil lubricant and displacement of the compressor slightly large and inside the compressor.
 
• Some plastic materials work well with HFC and POE oil.
 
• Now flush the evaporator, using dry nitrogen with sufficient pressure, and plug the ends.
 
• Change with a new condenser 20% extra larger and flush with dry nitrogen before connecting to the system.
 
• By using a newly developed capillary cutter, cut a new capillary tube, 20% larger than the existing size.
 
• Flush the capillary with dry nitrogen and immediately connect it to the system by brazing.
 
• Here new filter driver is used (molecular sieve type) which has greater moisture absorbing potential and molecular sieve filter drivers do not get pondered as in the case of silica gel driers used in CFC-12.
 
• Connect the new filter to the system and braze all the joints and pressurize the system using dry nitrogen by giving sufficient pressure and checking leaks in the system using soap solution. And make 100% sure that there is no leak in the system.

questions.question: Capillary tube is the expansion valve used in Refrigeration and Air Conditioning units _______.

questions.solution:
__**Explanation:**__

**Capillary tube:**

 
• The capillary tube is the most commonly used metering device on small refrigeration and air conditioning systems.
 
• It is used on virtually all domestic refrigerators and window air conditioners.
 
• **The capillary tube is the expansion valve used in refrigeration and Air Conditioning units with less than a 3-ton cooling capacity.**
 
• The function of capillary tube:
 
 
• To meter, the amount of refrigerant admitted to the evaporator. There must be sufficient to pick up and the heat working to be removed but not so much that the evaporator is filled with liquid.
 
• To regulate the pressure of the refrigerant and thus help maintain the evaporator at its designed temperature.
 
 
 
• The capillary tube consists of a long small diameter copper tube.
 
• As the liquid from the condenser is pushed through such a small passage, the friction between the refrigerant and the tube causes a pressure drop.
 
• When this pressure drop causes the flashing of the liquid to occur, the additional space occupied by the flash gas causes the pressure drop to increase rapidly.
 
• The capillary tube is commonly much longer than the distance from the condenser to the evaporator, the excess length is accommodated by rolling the capillary tube into a coil, extreme care must be taken not to Knik the capillary tube.
 
• This may be avoided by using any solid cylindrical shape as a form to wrap the capillary around a tin can to be used.
 
• The advantage of a capillary tube as a metering device is inexpensive and has no moving parts.
 
• Because it cannot change in order to match the different amounts of refrigerant that may be flowing through the system, however, its use is restricted to those systems that have a relatively constant load.

questions.question: Convert 2-Ton refrigeration to horsepower (metric).

• The cooling effect is measured by a unit known as a ton of refrigeration.

• If it is remembered that the latent heat of fusion is 144 BTU per pound, it follows that the ton represents a unit cooling effect of 144 x 2000 or 2,88,000 BTU per 24 hours.

= (288000~BTU)/(24~ hours)~=~12000~BTU/hr 

 
• Thus for air conditioning calculation the size of the required condensing unit expressed in tons can be obtained by dividing the heat gain of the structure, expressed in BTU per hour by 12000.

∴ Refrigeration in tons = (BTU~per~hour~heat~gain)/(12000)

 
• One refrigeration ton is equal to 3.5168525 kilowatts (or) 3.516 kW.

questions.question: Which is not the type of air conditioner compressor?

**Compressor:**

 
• A compressor is a mechanical device that increases the pressure of a gas by reducing its volume.
 
• An air compressor is a specific type of gas compressor.
 
• Compressors are similar to pumps: both increase the pressure on a fluid and both can transport the fluid through a pipe.
 
• The main distinction is that the focus of a compressor is to change the density or volume of the fluid

**The Five Main Types of Air Conditioning Compressors:**

 
• Reciprocating Air Conditioner Compressor
 
• Scroll air Conditioning Compressor
 
• Screw air Conditioning Compressor
 
• Rotary Air Conditioning Compressor
 
• Centrifugal Air Conditioning Compressor

**Rotary compressor:**

 
• A rotary compressor is a compressor in which gas is compressed in a rotary motion.
 
• Generally, it is used in small sealed systems like refrigerators and air conditioners.
 
• It is also used in vacuum pumps.
 
• The main parts of a stationary blade type rotary compressor are the roller spring and discharge valve, and the dividing blade is fitted on the cylinder wall.
 
• The roller is fixed on the shaft.
 
• The function of the dividing blade is separate low-pressure and high-pressure.
 
• The oil is filled in the outer dome.
 
• The oil level is maintained below the discharge tube.
 
• The shaft is connected to the motor.
 
• When the motor or the roller rotates through the surface of the cylinder, then low-pressure gas enters the cylinder and is compressed into the outer dome.
 
• Hence oil and gas will separate.
 
• The oil will collect at the outer dome and compressed gas flows into the discharge line.

**Scroll type compressor:**

 
• Scroll compressors are orbital motion, positive displacement machines that compress with two inter-fitting, spiral-shaped scroll members (one is fixed and another is movable).
 
• The motor stator is rigidly attached to the shell.
 
• The rotor is shrink-fit onto, the eccentric shaft.
 
• The shaft is supported by two bearings, one in the crankcase and the second below the motor.

**Centrifugal compressor:**

 
• A centrifugal compressor is also called a turbo or a radial compressor which compresses the refrigerant to high pressure and temperature by adding kinetic energy to the cool vapor refrigerant is forced to pass into and through the impeller, and the impeller forces the fluid to spin faster and faster.
 
• The high-speed refrigerant gas is then forced to pass through the diffuser where the refrigerant gas volume expands as its speed decrease.
 
• This process converts the kinetic energy of the high-speed low-pressure gas to low-speed higher-pressure gas.
 
• The higher the impeller speed, the higher the pressure.

• The relay has a coil that is connected in series with the main winding.

• After the motor reaches proper speed, the main winding current drops to a low value and causes the armature of the relay to fall downwards and open the contacts, thereby cutting out the auxiliary winding from the supply.
 
• Such relays are located outside the motor so that they can be easily serviced or replaced.

**Basic Vapor Absorption Refrigeration System:**

 
• The basic absorption cycle employs two fluids, the absorbate or refrigerant, and the absorbent.

• These fluids are separated and recombined in the absorption cycle.
 
• In the absorption cycle, the low-pressure refrigerant vapor is absorbed into the absorbent releasing a large amount of heat (Absorber pressure is equal to evaporator pressure).
 
• The liquid refrigerant/absorbent solution is pumped to a high-operating pressure generator using significantly less electricity than that for compressing the refrigerant for an electric chiller.
 
• Heat is added at the high-pressure generator from a gas burner, steam, hot water, or hot gases.

• The vapors flow to a condenser, where heat is rejected and condensed to a high-pressure liquid.
 
• The liquid is then throttled through an expansion valve to the lower pressure in the evaporator where it evaporates by absorbing heat and providing useful cooling.
 
• The remaining liquid absorbent, in the generator, passes through a valve, where its pressure is reduced, and then is recombined with the low-pressure refrigerant vapors returning from the evaporator so the cycle can be repeated.

questions.question: Which is the best way of checking leak of split A/C condenser installed unit?

questions.question: De-scaling of condenser is the process of _______ cleaning.

• Ensure that the inlet and outlet valves are opened and regained pressure drop is indicated between the inlet and outlet water pressure gauges mounted on the condenser.

questions.question: Thermal resistance of an ideal conductor would be _________.
questions.solution:
__**Explanation:**__

**Thermal resistance:**

 
• Thermal resistance is a heat property and a measurement of a temperature difference by which an object or material resists a heat flow.
 
• Thermal resistance is the reciprocal of thermal conductance.
 
• Absolute thermal resistance is the temperature difference across a structure when a unit of heat energy flows through it in unit time.
 
• It is the reciprocal of thermal conductance.
 
• The SI unit of absolute thermal resistance is kelvins per watt (K / W) or the equivalent degrees Celsius per watt (°C/W).
 
• Thermal resistance = (L)/(k~times~A) (Using Fourier's law of heat conduction)
 
• Where, L is the length of the material (measured on a path parallel to the heat flow) (m), k is the thermal conductivity of the material (W/K-m), A is the cross-sectional area (perpendicular to the path of heat flow) (m²)
 
• **The thermal resistance of the perfect conductor is zero.**
 
• A steady current in the perfect conductor will flow without losing energy to resistance.
 
• Resistance is what induces heating in the conductors because the ideal conductor does not produce heat.
 
• Because energy is not lost to heat, the current does not dissipate; it will continuously flow inside the perfect conductor until there is no thermal difference.
 
• **A perfect conductor is an idealized substance of infinite thermal conductivity and zero thermal resistivity.**

• It is applicable for ammonia refrigerant vapor.
 
• When it is exposed to air containing ammonia vapor, it gives off a white cloud of ammonium chloride or ammonium sulfite.
 
• The drawback of this method, it cannot be used to pinpoint leaks.

Litmus paper:

 
• This is also applicable to ammonia.
 
• When it is exposed to ammonia vapor, moist red litmus paper will turn blue.
 
• The drawback of this method, it cannot be used with any halogen family refrigerants.

Bubble tests:

 
• This method is followed in most common areas on pipes and fittings.
 
• Soapy water (mixture of soap and water) will indicate the locations of leaks by the formation of bubbles escaping the gas/vapor/air.
 
• The drawback of this method is applicable to the pressure of the system more than atmospheric pressure (1.01325 bar).
 
• When test solutions are applied to low temperature, low pressure (below atmospheric level) suction lines could cause considerable damage; due to which the test solution could be drawn into the system.

Halide test lamp/Halide torch:

 
• This kind of leak detection is used to locate fluro-carbon refrigerant leaks by the fuel like propane, butane, or methylated spirits which is filled into the fuel tank.
 
• The fuel tank supplies pressurized fuel at a steady and controlled pressure and a jet admits the fuel to a burner.
 
• When lit, the burner flame is supported by oxygen in the air which is drawn through a tube used as a sensing probe.
 
• The probe is passed slowly over the joints or surfaces being leak tested.
 
• If any fluro-carbon refrigerants are drawn into the tube, the color of the lamp flame will change to green or blue depending on the quantity of gas passed over the burner element.

Direct online (DOL) starter:

 
• A DOL starter is a method of starting a 3-phase induction motor.
 
• In a DOL Starter, an induction motor is connected directly across its 3-phase supply, and the DOL starter applies the full line voltage to the motor terminals.

Motor starting characteristics on DOL starter:

 
• Available starting current: 100%
 
• Peak starting current: 6 to 8 times full load current
 
• Peak starting torque: 100%

**Working of DOL starter:**

 
• The main heart of the DOL starter is the relay coil.
 
• **The mechanical relay fits with the DOL starter.**
 
• Normally it gets one phase constant from incoming supply volts.
 
• When the coil gets second phase relay coil energizes and the magnet of the contactor produces an electromagnetic field due to this, the plunger of the contactor will move and the main contactor of the starter will be closed and the auxiliary will change its position.

Advantages of DOL starter:

 
• The most economical and cheapest starter
 
• Simple to establish, operate, and maintain
 
• Simple control circuitry
 
• Easy to understand and troubleshoot.
 
• It provides 100% torque at the time of starting.
 
• Only one set of cables is required from the starter to the motor.
 
• The motor is connected in the delta at motor terminals.

**DOL is suitable for:**

 
• A direct online starter can be used if the high inrush current of the motor does not cause an excessive voltage drop in the supply circuit.
 
• The maximum size of the motor allowed on a direct on Line starter may be limited by the supply utility for this reason.
 
• For example, a utility may require rural customers to use reduced-voltage starters for motors larger than 10 kW.
 
• DOL starting is sometimes used to start small water pumps, compressors, fans, and conveyor belts.

questions.question: Which type of compressor is used for domestic air conditioner?
questions.solution:
__Explanation:__

Domestic refrigerator:

 
• The domestic refrigerator uses a **Hermetically sealed** compressor.
 
• The compressor constricts the refrigerant vapor, raising its pressure and temperature, and pushes it into the coils of the condenser on the outside of the refrigerator.
 
• The refrigerant absorbs the heat inside the fridge when it flows through the evaporator coils, cooling down the air inside the fridge.

Hermetic compressor:

 
• Usually, hermetic or sealed type provides compact assembly will require less place and is noiseless.
 
• The unit is completely sealed in and tested at the factory, trouble-free with compressor motor assembly.
 
• The motor located above the compressor operates horizontally.
 
• This construction method permits the operation of the compressor in oil, simplifying the lubricating problem.
 
• The suction intake is placed so that suction vapor must travel through the holes in the motor rotor in order to get to the top of the shell and then to the intake tube.
 
• Any oil or liquid refrigerant is separated from the vapor by centrifugal force due to the rotation of the motor rotor as the vapor passes up through the holes in the rotor.
 
• Consequently, oil and liquid separation assured oil is eliminated, and with it, damage to the valve breakage coil is picked up in a small slot on the end of the crankshaft which acts as a centrifugal pump, and the oil is forced into the power main bearing.
 
• From this point it follows the spiral groove in the bearing up to the crankcase where it lubricates the trust plate, connecting rod and piston coil are then pumped through a tube by vapor action up to a small reservoir beside the upper main bearing and is then fed into and spiraled up through the bearing from where it drops back to the sump.
 
• The main parts of the reciprocating compressor are the head plate valve plate and valves, piston, piston pin, connecting rod, and crankshaft.
 
• In the hermetic type, there is no need for the shaft seal.
 
• The compressor and motor have a common shaft and are assembled in a single body and the whole assembled is fixed in a steel shell, the joints of which are welded.
